description:
SYNTHETIC. Standard-library Python plus NumPy: symmetry entropy measures what a projection can resolve, what it must store, and what it is blind to. Five measured quantity families: (1) orbit entropy log2(|orbit|) under the dihedral group D4 on 4x4 patterns -- asymmetric patterns 3 bits, blocks 1 bit, ring and cross 0 bits (orbit collapse, the falsified design); (2) projection entropy, the Shannon entropy of the Born weights after projecting onto a stored subspace -- 0 bits for a clean stored Bell state, 0.618 bits at noise sigma 0.25, 1.270 bits at sigma 0.75, 1.581 bits for a Haar-random state (max log2 3 = 1.585 bits); (3) asymmetry cost S(twirl(rho)) - S(rho) under the Pauli group {I, X} -- |0> costs 1 bit = log2(2), |+> costs 0 bits = log2(1); (4) self-determinism factor D = <psi|P|psi>, the squared norm of a probe's projection onto the stored subspace -- D = 1 for a clean stored probe, 0 for a kernel probe (Psi-, all Born weights 0), strictly between for noisy and random probes (Phi+ sigma 0.25: 0.843; sigma 0.75: 0.567; Haar-random mean over 200 seeds 0.720). D is the denominator of the Born weights; (5) honeycomb / bee-hexagon extension -- D6 orbit entropy on 6-tuples (fully asymmetric hexagonal pattern 3.585 bits, honeycomb cell 0 bits), the honeycomb lattice (7-hexagon patch bipartite, 24 vertices, 30 edges, two triangular sublattices 12/12) and Hales efficiency (hexagon perimeter 3.7224 < square 4.0000 < triangle 4.5590 for unit area), the Shipman projection (a 6D flag manifold projects to a 2D hexagon; alpha-parameter curve family changes topology at alpha = 1/sqrt(3) = 0.5774), and the radical-pair compass toy (singlet yield depends on field strength and direction: 0.3763 along z vs 0.2524 along x at 50 uT). Eight falsifiable claims, all measured: distinct recalls equal orbit size in closed-orbit mode; the projection kernel (Psi-, orthogonal to all stored patterns) is invisible with all Born weights 0; the projected world has higher entropy than the underlying state by the asymmetry cost, in the classical orbit case and the quantum twirl case; the projection is self-determined exactly to the extent the probe lies in the stored subspace; D6 orbit entropy bounds distinguishability; the hexagon has the least perimeter for unit area and the honeycomb patch is bipartite; the radical-pair singlet yield is magnetic-field-dependent in strength and direction; the Shipman alpha curve family changes topology at alpha = 1/sqrt(3). No headline claim is emitted. No speedup, no Bell violation, no hardware data, no claim about physical reality. Shipman is a documented correlation with an unproven mechanism (geometry measured, not the bee's brain); the radical-pair model is a one-nucleus toy, not a measurement of a real bee's cryptochrome.

Acknowledgement: the vendored projection code derives from a package received under Mun Seok Lee's name (see the quantum-projection README Provenance section). No endorsement implied. Lee is inspiration only for the symmetry membrane.
